clue.text: E.g. Moscow correspondent’s writings in USSR, say

blocks.note: Moscow is an example of a capital city
what a correspondent writes and posts

explanation.surface: A foreign correspondent in Moscow files reports from the Soviet Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a journalist's dispatches, but 'E.g. Moscow' is just a capital city and the writings are mail. The definition sits at the end as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for the Soviet Union is printed entirely in upper-case type, so it serves as an example of such script.

clue.text: Dig up tree from the south, oddly missing needles here

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered positions gone, only the even-placed characters remain
in a down entry, reading from the bottom upward runs the string backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth characters of these words

explanation.surface: A gardener uproots a tree, leaving pine needles scattered about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig up tree' looks like an instruction but is only the source letters. An ETUI is a small ornamental case for needles and pins, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: This small decorative case traditionally holds sewing pins, so it is a place where such items are kept.

clue.text: The two of us, informally, giving option list

blocks.note: 'me and you', squeezed into text-message spelling with single letters for 'and' and 'you'

explanation.surface: A couple casually offering each other a list of choices.
explanation.walkthrough: In text-message spelling 'me and you' shrinks to ME N U, which runs together as MENU.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer or in a restaurant, this is the displayed list of choices from which a user picks.

clue.text: Queen American philosopher interrupts roughly

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: ca., short for circa, means approximately
John Stuart Mill, the utilitarian thinker

explanation.surface: A US thinker rudely cuts into a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a search for a real American thinker, but the nationality is a separate single letter and the philosopher is John Stuart Mill, who was English. 'Roughly' is the circa abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the wife of King Charles III and was crowned Queen consort in 2023.

clue.text: Fate of poor team helping to overwhelm English cricket side

indicators.note: overwhelming something engulfs it, so one piece swallows up the others

blocks.note: the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs

explanation.surface: A struggling sports team gets crushed by an English cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket side' suggests a team of players, but it is one half of the field, the side behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club finishing near the bottom of its league is demoted to a lower division at season's end.

clue.text: Least colourful painter entertains popular composer

indicators.note: a host who entertains has guests inside the house, so one piece holds another

explanation.surface: A drab artist plays host to a well-loved musician.
explanation.walkthrough: A member of the Royal Academy is the usual crossword painter, and 'popular' is the common short word for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was the great Italian Renaissance writer of sacred polyphonic church music.

clue.text: Represented Macbeth, say, with ease, considering the circumstances

indicators.note: represented means depicted in a new form, so the letters are rendered in another order

explanation.surface: An actor played Shakespeare's tragic Scottish king effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Macbeth, say' reads as an example of a role, but 'say' is part of the letter pool along with Macbeth and ease.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means depending on the situation, whichever applies in the particular instance.

clue.text: Plot by politicians creating fictions after retiring

blocks.note: a garden plot, as in a flower bed
as in multiplication, three by four
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A scheme by politicians to spin lies once they have left office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' and 'retiring' both point to politics, but the plot is a garden one and retiring means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tales read aloud to children as they settle down for the night, so invented narratives told on turning in.

clue.text: Wee drop of Drambuie, then four in 60 seconds

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter is taken
one item placed inside the other

blocks.note: one minute, written as I (one) and MINUTE

explanation.surface: A tiny dram of Scotch liqueur, followed by four more downed in a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur, so 'wee drop' looks like the measure, but 'Wee' is the definition. Sixty seconds is 'one minute', with one as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very small; wee is the Scottish informal term for tiny.

clue.text: Woman kept in order? Not a single one, it’s said

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so go by pronunciation

explanation.surface: A woman in a disciplined household; not one is unattached, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like discipline, but it is a religious order; and 'Not a single one' hints at being unmarried while just meaning none.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a female member of a religious community living under vows within a monastic institution.

clue.text: Little boy creating current agitation

blocks.note: first meaning: a pet form of Edward, a name for a small lad
second meaning: a swirl in moving water

explanation.surface: A small child stirring up trouble right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but means a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a familiar short form of Edward, and also a whirlpool or circular movement in a stream.

clue.text: He perhaps has dip from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, starting from the east means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A man, maybe, takes a swim heading westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun, but it is the chemical symbol for helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is an example of an inert vapour-state element at room temperature.

clue.text: Jack Anthony Fitzgerald who sang dance tune

blocks.note: both are slang for a sailor
the first three letters of the name, a common short form

explanation.surface: A man with three names who sang a dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: The three names read as one person, but each is separate. 'Who sang' points to the jazz singer rather than to the author F. Scott Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lively southern Italian folk dance in fast triple time, and the music written for it.

clue.text: Port Bezos’s assistant consumes along with fruit, occasionally

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens at intervals, so only every other character is kept
to consume is to take inside oneself, so one piece swallows others

blocks.note: Amazon's voice assistant; Jeff Bezos founded Amazon

explanation.surface: Jeff Bezos's aide eats port wine with some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink, but it is a harbour city. Alexa is Amazon's smart-speaker assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is the major Egyptian harbour city on the Mediterranean, founded by Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Presume working at a desk involves dealing with admin, primarily

indicators.note: working means in operation or being processed, so the letters are put to work in a new order
to involve is to include within, so one piece goes inside another
primarily means first of all, so only the initial character is kept

explanation.surface: Someone assumes that office work at a desk includes the paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working at a desk' reads as office life, but 'working' signals rearranging the next three words. RE and A sit inside, just before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something as true without needing it to be stated or proved is the idiomatic meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Get back from market with rug

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so the final character is taken

blocks.note: rug is slang for a toupee or hairpiece

explanation.surface: Coming home from the shops carrying a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back' looks like a phrasal verb meaning return; 'Get' alone is the definition, and 'rug' is the jokey word for a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage, to twig is to understand or catch on, the same as 'I get it'.

clue.text: Creative, impractical and rather risqué broadcaster

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite TV company

explanation.surface: A TV presenter who is imaginative, unrealistic and a bit naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads as three adjectives for one person, but the first two are the definition and the last two words are the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-sky thinking means imaginative ideas unconstrained by practical limits, often not yet workable.

clue.text: Did water sport around middle of lido in Split

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central characters, dropping the ends
going around something encloses it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: dived, as in diving into a pool

explanation.surface: Someone swam at an open-air pool while on holiday in the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like the Croatian resort; it is the definition. A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past forms meaning separated into parts or shared out between people.

clue.text: Irrelevant current message about BoJo, say

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the string runs backwards

blocks.note: symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A pointless topical memo concerning Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: BoJo is the nickname of Boris Johnson, the former UK Prime Minister, who went to Eton College, the elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson was educated at Eton, so he is an example of a former pupil of that school.

clue.text: Mount Everest and then Niagara on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the insides go and only the outer characters stay

explanation.surface: A holiday itinerary: climb Everest, then visit the Niagara Falls.
explanation.walkthrough: With two famous landmarks in view, 'Mount Everest' looks like one name, but 'Mount' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, so a mountain, matching the abbreviated title used before peak names.

clue.text: E.g. pages in books covered with data sent out

indicators.note: something covered is wrapped on the outside, so one piece encloses another
out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters need rearranging

blocks.note: New Testament, the books of the later Bible

explanation.surface: Pages within books are wrapped up with emailed information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pages in books' looks like sheets of paper, but pages here are young servants. NT goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a boy employed to run errands or wait on someone, so an example of servants who wait upon others.

clue.text: Vocally curse woman who has children

indicators.note: vocally means spoken with the voice, so pronunciation matters, not spelling

explanation.surface: A mother swears out loud at her kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent N drops away when spoken. The definition stretches a word usually used of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the term for a mother, chiefly of livestock such as horses, and archaically for a human parent.

clue.text: Does this suggest singular rather than plural refusals?

definitions.text: Does this suggest singular rather than plural refusals?

blocks.clueFragment: Does this suggest singular rather than plural
blocks.note: surface reading: a grammar question about number
setter's reading: the word for several negative replies, which split as two words says 'lacking the plural ending'

explanation.surface: A grammarian's puzzled question about plural forms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as NO S, the answer seems to say there is no S, which would mean singular; yet the word is itself the plural of no.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one accepted plural spelling for negative answers or votes against.

clue.text: A Wimbledon favourite spotted speaking incorrectly?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ranked player kept apart in the draw
second meaning: a dialect or ungrammatical past tense of see

explanation.surface: A tennis favourite was seen mispronouncing words.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London grass-court tennis championship. 'Speaking incorrectly' marks the non-standard 'I seed it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Top tennis players are ranked to avoid meeting early; and in some dialects the past tense of see is formed irregularly.

clue.text: Criminal errs, a woman PC’s possible extortioner

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A woman police constable may have a blackmailer on her hands.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like police constable, but it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: This malicious software locks a computer's files and demands payment for their release, so it extorts money from a machine's owner.

clue.text: Drop writing implement taken from Open University

indicators.note: something taken from a thing is removed from it

explanation.surface: A student abandons a pen borrowed from the Open University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' reads as the UK distance-learning institution, but it splits into two words treated separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to leave something out or exclude it from a list.

clue.text: Makes vows in the middle of the working week

definitions.text: the middle of the working week

blocks.clueFragment: the middle of the working week
blocks.note: second meaning: the abbreviation for the midweek day

explanation.surface: A couple tie the knot midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' tempts you to take central letters, but it describes the third of five weekdays.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to take wedding promises; and the short form for Wednesday names the central weekday.

clue.text: A faff after a military corps defends attack very well

indicators.note: defenders form a ring around what they protect, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: the Special Air Service, the British special forces regiment
a sudden bout, as in a fit of coughing
to faff is to fiddle about

explanation.surface: A fuss follows when an army unit repels an assault superbly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the opening words at the end. Faff is British slang for fuss or messing about.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in excellent health, so it is a jaunty way of saying someone is in good shape.
